title: Prepared-solve first-convergence versus fixed-response continuation diagnosis
bounded_conclusions: The G21A path effect is not a transient first-convergence-report artifact that disappears under additional identical-response solve calls.
The fresh arm reaches the frozen fresh-response head on its first solve call, reports convergence on call 2, and remains bitwise stationary at the middle cell through call 12.
The history arm approaches a different fixed head after the outer-1 response history. It first reports convergence on outer-2 call 6 with a 7.235179122488944e-11 m offset from the fresh solution.
Six further identical-response calls after that convergence report change the history head by only 6.66e-16 m in total; the call-12 path offset remains 7.235112509107466e-11 m.

After first convergence, each history head-vector update is only 1.11e-16 m while MODFLOW continues to report convergence. The offset therefore behaves as persistent prepared-solve path memory at the strict G21 scale.

XOLD remains bitwise fixed and HCOF/RHS are identical between fresh and history arms, so the measured difference is associated with other path-dependent prepared-solve state or finite-precision nonlinear assembly/history, not accepted-origin drift or response differences.
G21 remains falsified. G21B is diagnostic evidence only and does not redefine MODFLOW convergence or authorize post-convergence solve calls as production behavior.
next_natural_unit: Open G21C as a read-only state-forensics diagnostic. Compare accessible MODFLOW/XMI state and package arrays between FRESH and HISTORY at the identical fixed response and converged heads to identify which non-XOLD state retains path memory. Prefer existing exposed arrays and source-backed semantics; do not add a production state-reset primitive.
